title_candidates: Coding agents make small device automations worth trying
A safer way to try AI-assisted device automation
summary: Coding agents are lowering the effort behind one-off device automations. Start safely with official app actions, a public manual, and one reversible shortcut.

primary_source.title: Reverse-engineering is cheap now
primary_source.author: Simon Willison
key_facts: Willison reports hearing about people using coding agents to understand and automate devices in their homes.
He presents these projects as an example of how cheaper code changes which small automations are worth attempting.
Device reverse-engineering was possible before coding agents, but the effort often outweighed the value of a one-off result.
Undocumented device interfaces can change, leaving owners with an ongoing maintenance burden.
Coding agents reduce both the initial effort and the cost of an experiment that does not work.

quote_candidates.text: Coding agents change that equation entirely.

supporting_sources.title: Navigate the action list in Shortcuts on iPhone or iPad
key_facts: Apple documents how installed apps expose actions that people can use in Shortcuts without discovering or calling private device interfaces.

supporting_sources.title: File Uploads FAQ
key_facts: OpenAI documents file uploads in ChatGPT; the guide limits uploads to public manuals and excludes credentials or device identifiers.

prerequisites: An iPhone or iPad with Apple Shortcuts
A device you own with an official companion app
An AI assistant that accepts documents

steps.instruction: Download only the device's public manual from its manufacturer; exclude serial numbers, account details, Wi-Fi credentials, pairing codes, API keys, and diagnostic logs.
Open Shortcuts, navigate to App Shortcuts, and note the exact actions exposed by the device's official app. If none appear, stop rather than probing private interfaces.

Upload the public manual to your AI assistant, paste the official action names, and ask for one manually run, reversible shortcut using only those actions. Exclude private APIs, network scanning, credentials, and security bypasses.
In App Shortcuts, use the suggested official action in a new shortcut named 'Device test'. Keep it manual; do not add time, location, voice, or unattended triggers.

Stand beside the device, run the shortcut once, confirm the expected harmless result, and undo any change in the official app. Delete it if the result differs or creates a safety, warranty, privacy, household, or cost concern.

risk_flags: The primary post is an observation, not a measured study of coding-agent productivity.
Reverse-engineering can create safety, security, warranty, privacy, and legal risks; the guide uses only official app actions for a device the reader owns.
Public manuals should be checked for personal identifiers before upload, and users should review their AI provider's data controls.
